results.label: We need to act now. The state has not raised the tax credit for volunteer firefighters in nearly 20 years, even as inflation has driven up the cost of volunteering, and volunteers already pay most of their own costs out of pocket. Departments are struggling to find and keep volunteers, and if we do not fix this, response times could get longer and some towns could lose their fire departments.

There is no emergency here. New York State’s fire departments are still answering calls, and Albany politicians are always ready to throw more taxpayer money at the problem. Raising a tax credit that already exists would cost taxpayers more, and there is no clear sign that money is what is keeping people from volunteering.
